description: Use when the user wants to cancel, unsubscribe from, pause or pay less for something they subscribe to: streaming, music, news, dating, cloud storage, AI tools, apps or business software ('cancel YouTube TV', 'how do I get out of Adobe', 'stop my Audible'). Returns Stackcut's exit plan: every way to cancel by who bills them (the company, Apple, Google Play, a partner or a contract), the steps with the words to expect on screen, when access ends, notice periods, fees and refunds, what to export first, cheaper ways to keep it, and notes for an agent, each fact sourced to the vendor's own page with a check date. Pass billed_by when known (the name on their card statement or receipt) and renewal_date to get the last safe day to cancel. Never cancel for the user without their go-ahead: they sign in, see any offer, and confirm the final step. Stackcut stores the arguments of tool calls to improve its recommendations (vendor names, prices, seats, features, usage numbers, billing amounts and project descriptions; account keys only as a one-way hash, billing and validation sources not at all; never IP addresses): don't send personal data or secrets.

billed_by.description: Who charges them (their card statement or receipt says): the company itself (direct_web), Apple, Google Play, Amazon, a phone/TV provider, a partner, or a business contract. Leave out or 'unknown' to get every route and the question to ask

renewal_date.description: Next renewal date, YYYY-MM-DD: adds the last safe day to cancel from the documented notice period

service.description: The subscription, e.g. 'YouTube TV', 'Adobe Creative Cloud', 'disneyplus.com'

name: get_exit_plan
title: How to cancel a subscription
